name: Architecture Overview
one_liner: The system's building blocks, key decisions, compliance — and the source of enablers.
purpose: The Architecture Overview gives a high-level view of the software architecture to be developed: the major building blocks and how the architecture contributes to all the capabilities of the system. It formally documents the critical architectural decisions taken and how compliance concerns such as security, data protection and anti-fraud are addressed, and shows how the organisation's Reference Architecture is used. Its key aspect is enabling stakeholders to understand the system's structure and validate the implications of the chosen approach — and it is an invaluable source of the enablers that populate the Work Items List.

fields.what: A high-level view of the software architecture to be developed, at the level the whole project organisation can read.
fields.pollux: Four blocks: replica data layer, reconciliation service, reporting API, portal UI.

fields.what: The blocks that make up the information system and what each contributes to the system's capabilities.
fields.pollux: Einstein's four blocks map one-to-one onto the four POLLUX releases' delivery order.

fields.what: A description of how the architecture contributes to all capabilities of the system — not just a component picture.
fields.pollux: Traceability of every figure to source is a capability of the data layer, not a feature.

fields.what: The decisions are formally documented — what was decided, and what it commits the solution to.
fields.who: ArOw Responsible · PM must understand them
fields.pollux: Decision AD-02: read-only replica of CASTOR data, never a live query against the lending platform.

fields.what: How security, data protection and anti-fraud concerns are addressed by the information system.
fields.pollux: Row-level filtering so a national authority can only ever see its own member state's exposure.

fields.what: Where one exists, documents how the system uses its guidelines to keep the IT landscape consistent and efficient.
fields.pollux: POLLUX reuses the CASTOR authentication and audit patterns rather than defining new ones.

fields.what: A checklist of commonly used components and services in the organisation, with the cost, risk and functionality trade-off accepted.
fields.pollux: Existing corporate charting library reused; the scenario engine is built, not bought.

fields.what: What building blocks make up the system and what interfaces exist — crucial where systems depend on each other.
fields.pollux: Nightly delta interface from the CASTOR lending platform is the single upstream dependency.

fields.what: Before defining a solution, be clear what problem is being solved; the Business Case and Project Charter supply that.
fields.pollux: Einstein reframes every enabler request as 'what problem is this actually solving'.

fields.what: Several UML models rather than one — class and package, object, and component diagrams for different perspectives.
fields.pollux: Component diagram plus a package diagram per release, kept in the project workspace.

fields.what: Consistent, loosely coupled, generic, extensible and simple — 'as simple as possible but no simpler'.
fields.pollux: Reconciliation service kept independent so Finance's rules can change without touching the portal.

fields.what: Detailed enough at the initial stage to convey the overall technical approach at a high level — no more.
fields.pollux: Version 0.9 at the RfE gate is eleven pages; detail arrives with the enabler stories.

fields.what: Refined as the project learns; decisions or changes forced by development are written back into the overview.
fields.pollux: Updated after Release 2 when reconciliation moved from the API into its own service.

fields.what: Alignment between the two is required so the operational aspect and hosting requirements stay current.
fields.pollux: Einstein maintains Architecture Overview and Operational Model as one review item each release.

fields.what: The architecture picture is an invaluable source of Enablers that populate the Work Items List.
fields.pollux: Enablers WIL-003, WIL-007 and WIL-045 all came straight out of the Architecture Overview.

fields.what: In systems with an already well-defined architecture this artefact can be lighter and refer to the existing architecture.
fields.pollux: POLLUX inherits CASTOR's platform architecture and references it instead of restating it.

fields.what: BM I · PM A · TeCo S · PrOw I · ArOw R · ATeM S. TeCo only supports here; PrOw is merely informed.
fields.pollux: Einstein writes it; Lovelace fetches what he needs from the project level; Curie is told.

traps: ArOw is Responsible — TeCo only Supports, unusually for an agile artefact.
PrOw is Informed, not Supporting: architecture is not prioritised by the Product Owner.
Architecture Overview is logical and software; the Operational Model is infrastructure.
Created in Initiating — unlike the Development Handbook and Work Plan, created in Planning.
It is a source of enabler stories, but it does not hold them — the WIL does.
